newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Irish woman jailed in Cyprus for false rape claim.
newsitem.headline: Irish woman jailed in Cyprus for false rape claim.

text.p: An Irish woman was jailed for four months in Cyprus on Friday for filing a false complaint to police that she was raped by three Irishmen, police and judicial sources said.

Tourist Annette Mangan, 22, of 44 Castle Park, Dublin, pleaded guilty to charges of filing a false complaint when local police found discrepancies in her claim the three men raped her at the holiday resort of Ayia Napa on Thursday morning.
Mangan reported her fictionary rape to police on Thursday, but doctors who examined her at a local government hospital found no signs of rape.
She retracted her statement hours later, admitting she wanted to get her own back on them for photographing her having sex with another Irishman she met on Wednesday night.
All four men were staying in the same apartment.
Mangan appeared calm as the district court of Famagusta passed sentence but her sister and two friends wept, witnesses said.

Two of the men were soldiers. Paul Hogan, 27, and Noel Higgins, 22, are members of the Irish contingent of UNIFIL, the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon. They were on holiday in Cyprus. The third man detained and later released was Kevin Moore, 21, a tourist.
The soldiers spent eight hours in a jail cell but were released when Mangan confessed she lied, police said.
Mangan told police she wanted to "get back" at the soldiers, who allegedly shot pictures of her as she was having sex with the fourth Irishman, also a tourist.
"She was confused because they took photographs of her naked and she felt humiliated. She was raped psychologically, not physically," lawyer Kyriakos Chitchos told the court.
He said she ended up in the apartment after a night of "merriment and drinking".
"Revenge does her no honour but she has shown remorse," he added.
District judge Antonis Liatsos criticised Mangan. "Innocent people were arrested and held in custody and grievances on their detention are fully justified," said Liatsos.

"The excuse of the accused that she did not want them to photograph her naked is not accepted...the penalty must be a deterrent. The girl is young and will stay away from her country, but the indicative sentence under the circumstances is four months in jail."
